title: A hotel-scoped users.manage holder can grant all_hotels=true (to anyone, including themself) and so escape their own hotel allow-list
lower_trust_principal: Staff user with users.manage whose all_hotels=false (allowed to hotel A only)
boundary_crossed: Hotel boundary inside a group (allowedHotelIds), and role boundary (any role incl. group-owner assignable)

entrypoint.description: PATCH /api/v1/users/{user} (update) and POST /api/v1/users (store, line 100); only checks users.manage and same group_id

sink.description: $user->update(collect($data)->only(['name','status','all_hotels'])) and syncRoles($data['roles']) with no check that the actor themself has all_hotels or holds the role being granted

propagation.description: store(): 'all_hotels' => ['boolean'] accepted from body
store(): User::create([... 'all_hotels' => $data['all_hotels'] ?? false])
update(): 'roles' => any role name that exists for guard api (e.g. group-owner, finance-director)
allowedHotelIds() is recomputed from DB on every request, so the escalation is effective immediately
Hotel index/global scope then returns every hotel of the group

intended_control: Per-user hotel allow-list (users.hotels pivot / all_hotels) is the second tenancy dimension; a hotel manager should not be able to widen it beyond their own scope nor hand out higher roles
observed_or_expected_result: Hotel-A manager PATCHes their own user (or a colleague) with {"all_hotels": true, "roles": ["group-owner"]} -> next request they read/write every hotel of the group (reservations, folios, payroll, accounting) and hold group-owner permissions
conditions: actor has users.manage (hotel manager role likely has it)
actor is not all_hotels (otherwise nothing to gain except role escalation)
update() does not exclude the actor's own user id
smallest_fix: In store()/update(): abort_unless($request->user()->all_hotels, 403) when all_hotels is requested true; restrict hotel_ids to the actor's allowedHotelIds(); forbid assigning roles the actor does not hold (or require a group-level permission such as users.manage_group); forbid editing own account's scope/roles
regression_test_idea: Feature test: user A (all_hotels=false, hotels=[A], role hotel-manager with users.manage) PATCH /api/v1/users/{A} {all_hotels:true} -> 403 and allowedHotelIds unchanged; PATCH with roles:[group-owner] -> 403

title: Scheduled report edited by another user still runs with the creator's identity and hotel allow-list
lower_trust_principal: Staff user with reports.manage at hotel H (e.g. limited hotel scope, lower role)
boundary_crossed: User identity / permission boundary (report runs as original creator, e.g. finance director with all_hotels)

entrypoint.description: PUT /api/v1/scheduled-reports/{scheduledReport}: any reports.manage user of the hotel can change report, params, recipients

sink.description: Auth::guard('api')->setUser($creator); ctx->set($s->group_id,$s->hotel_id,$creator->allowedHotelIds(),$creator); then exporter renders the report through InternalApi as that user and mails it to $s->recipients

propagation.description: fill(validated) never resets created_by to the editor
POST .../run lets the editor trigger it immediately
'recipients.*' => email : attacker-controlled destination; 'report' => any key in ReportRegistry; 'params' free array
sub-request user resolver = creator, so permission checks in the underlying report controller pass with the creator's rights

intended_control: Comment in Exporter/InternalApi: 'a document or export is only ever as visible as the resource it is built from' (checked for the caller) - but the caller at run time is the creator, not the editor
observed_or_expected_result: User B (reports.manage, hotel-limited, no payroll/accounting permission) edits a report created by the finance director: sets report to a payroll/accounting export and recipients to B's address, calls /run -> receives data B is not allowed to read
conditions: ScheduledReport is hotel-scoped, so B must share the hotel with the creator
any ReportRegistry key whose underlying endpoint B lacks permission for
smallest_fix: On update(): set created_by = $request->user()->id (re-own the report) or forbid editing reports created by others; on run(): execute as $request->user() instead of created_by
regression_test_idea: User B without accounting.view updates a director-created scheduled report to report='general-ledger' + recipients=[b@x] and POSTs /run -> expect 403 / last_status failed, no mail sent

title: Webhook subscription accepts any hotel_id (or null = whole group) without checking the actor's allowed hotels
lower_trust_principal: Staff user with integrations.manage limited to hotel A

entrypoint.description: POST /api/v1/webhooks: 'hotel_id' => ['nullable','integer'] - no exists/allowed check; null means all hotels

sink.description: subscriptions matched by group_id and (hotel_id null OR hotel_id = event.hotel_id) -> deliveries of hotel B's events are queued to the attacker's URL

propagation.description: WebhookSubscription::create($data + secret) stamps group_id from context; hotel_id taken verbatim
delivery job posts the event envelope (payload with reservation/guest/invoice data) to the subscriber URL

intended_control: Per-user hotel allow-list; cross-group is already prevented by the group_id filter in QueueWebhookDeliveries
observed_or_expected_result: Hotel-A-only integrator creates {url: attacker, event_types:['*'], hotel_id: <hotel B id>} or hotel_id omitted -> receives all domain events (bookings, folio, payments, HR) of hotel B / the whole group
conditions: actor has integrations.manage
actor's all_hotels=false (otherwise group-wide access is legitimate)
smallest_fix: Validate hotel_id with Rule::exists('hotels','id')->where('group_id',$groupId) and, when actor->allowedHotelIds() !== null, require hotel_id in that list (and disallow null)
regression_test_idea: Hotel-A user with integrations.manage POST /webhooks hotel_id=B -> 422; hotel_id null -> 422 (or auto-set to active hotel)

title: Edge push tenant check for child tables passes when the parent row belongs to another hotel of the same group
lower_trust_principal: Edge node of hotel A (signed edge token; a compromised on-premise box or stolen node secret)
boundary_crossed: Hotel boundary within the group (edge node context is [hotel A] only)

entrypoint.description: POST /api/v1/edge/sync/push (public route, node signature) with changes[].table/row_id/data chosen by the node

propagation.description: if (! $p || (int)($p['hotel_id'] ?? 0) !== $node->hotel_id && (int)($p['group_id'] ?? 0) !== $node->group_id) - because && binds tighter than ||, a parent in hotel B of the same group (group matches) is NOT rejected
PARENTS: pos_check_lines, purchase_order_lines, goods_receipt_lines, stock_count_lines, purchase_requisition_lines, reservation_nights, room_block_allocations, loyalty_transactions, loyalty_cards
op=delete -> RowStore::delete for operational tables (reservation_nights, pos_check_lines, loyalty_cards...); upsert overwrites amounts/quantities

intended_control: tenantViolation() comment: 'an edge cannot take over a row owned by another tenant'; edge context set to [$node->hotel_id]
observed_or_expected_result: Node of hotel A pushes {table:'reservation_nights', row_id:<night of hotel B reservation>, op:'upsert', data:{id, reservation_id:<B res>, amount:0}} -> accepted ('applied'), hotel B's night revenue rewritten; or op:'delete' on hotel B pos_check_lines / loyalty_cards (loyalty_transactions is append-only but insert of a fake earn row for a B membership is possible since loyalty_memberships is group-level)
conditions: attacker controls an active edge node secret of any hotel in the group
target child table in TablePolicy::PARENTS
row data omits hotel_id/group_id keys (the tables have none)
smallest_fix: Parenthesise: if (! $p || ((int)($p['hotel_id'] ?? 0) !== $node->hotel_id && ! (array_key_exists('hotel_id',$p) === false && (int)($p['group_id'] ?? 0) === $node->group_id))) i.e. require hotel match when the parent has a hotel_id column, group match only for group-level parents (loyalty_memberships)
regression_test_idea: Unit test CloudSync::push with node(hotel A) and a change on reservation_nights whose reservation belongs to hotel B (same group) -> expect conflict 'tenant_rejected', row unchanged

title: Edge pull sends every group-level row (hotel_id null) incl. users rows with password/pos_pin hashes and encrypted MFA secrets of all hotels' staff to each node
boundary_crossed: Hotel boundary within group (staff credentials of hotel B replicated to hotel A's on-prem DB)

entrypoint.description: pull(): edge_changes where hotel_id = node.hotel_id OR (hotel_id null AND group_id = node.group_id)

sink.description: RowStore::read returns the full raw row (no $hidden filtering) for each change

propagation.description: 'users' is a replicated master table; users has group_id only, so its changes are group-level
columns password, pos_pin (hashed), mfa_secret (encrypted with APP_KEY), mfa_recovery_codes

intended_control: Edge node context is restricted to its own hotel ([$node->hotel_id]); users are per-hotel scoped via pivot
observed_or_expected_result: Operator of hotel A's edge box can dump users of hotel B (emails, bcrypt hashes, recovery codes) and attempt offline cracking; not verified whether ChangeCapture records users at all (only capture of models with group_id)
conditions: ChangeCapture logs users table changes with hotel_id null (not verified in this pass)
attacker has DB access on the edge box
smallest_fix: In ChangeFeed/RowStore::read strip sensitive columns for 'users' (password, pos_pin, mfa_secret, mfa_recovery_codes, remember_token) or restrict users replication to users allowed on the node's hotel (StaffDirectory::query)
regression_test_idea: Pull as node A after a user of hotel B changes -> payload must not contain password/mfa_secret and must not include users not allowed on hotel A

title: Guest data-protection export and merge read/re-point reservations and loyalty rows of every hotel in the group, ignoring the actor's allowed hotels
lower_trust_principal: Staff user with guests.manage limited to hotel A

sink.description: DB::table('reservations')->where('guest_id',$g->id)->get() and loyalty_memberships: raw query, no hotel_id / allowed-hotel filter, returns full rows of sister hotels (rates, dates, notes, totals)

propagation.description: merge(): DB::table($table)->where('guest_id',$dup->id)->update(guest_id) across reservations/folios/invoices of all hotels - a hotel-A user can rewrite hotel B's folio/invoice ownership
contrast: history()/folios() apply scoped() with allowedHotelIds - the intended pattern

intended_control: GuestProfileController::scoped() limits raw guest reads to the actor's allowed hotels
observed_or_expected_result: Hotel-A receptionist with guests.manage exports a VIP guest and obtains their complete stay history and amounts at hotel B; merge lets them silently re-assign hotel B invoices/folios to another guest
conditions: actor has guests.manage
actor all_hotels=false
smallest_fix: Reuse the scoped() helper (group_id + whereIn hotel_id allowed) for export; in merge() either require all_hotels or restrict the re-pointing updates to allowed hotels
regression_test_idea: Hotel-A user exports a guest with a hotel-B reservation -> response.reservations contains only hotel-A rows

title: Public booking lookup turns a guessable confirmation number + surname into a manage token (cancel/modify/pay) and leaks loyalty number and points balance
boundary_crossed: Guest-to-guest boundary inside a group's public booking site

sink.description: returns manage_token, guest name, special_requests, deposit figures, loyalty number/tier/points, online check-in ID type

propagation.description: number lookup over the whole group by confirmation number (sequenced per hotel, per comment)
distinct responses: 404 when number unknown, 404 name mismatch (same here) but 422 'ambiguous' when number exists in several hotels - partial oracle
cancel() accepts the manage_token obtained above

intended_control: Lookup credential = confirmation + last name; the 8-char public_code is the intended unguessable reference
observed_or_expected_result: Attacker iterates sequential confirmation numbers with common Cameroonian surnames (20 req/min/IP, no per-booking lockout) to obtain manage tokens, cancel competitors' bookings (fee charged to guest) and harvest loyalty balances
conditions: confirmation numbers are gapless sequences (NumberSequence)
attacker has many IPs or patience
surname distribution skewed
smallest_fix: Require the public_code (reference) or confirmation + last name + arrival date; add per-number failure counter/lockout; do not return loyalty points/number from lookup
regression_test_idea: lookup with number + wrong surname 5 times -> subsequent correct attempt blocked for N minutes; lookup response must not contain 'loyalty.points'

title: Member sign-up links the new account to any guest whose phone ends with the same 9 digits
lower_trust_principal: Anonymous person who controls a phone number
boundary_crossed: Guest-to-guest boundary (member account gets guest_id of another person's profile and thus their bookings, invoices, points)

entrypoint.description: POST /account/register then /account/register/verify (OTP to the attacker's own phone)

sink.description: matchGuest: whereRaw("length(digits) >= 9 and right(digits, 9) = ?", [last 9 digits]) - different country code / prefix with same trailing 9 digits matches; then account->guest_id = that guest

propagation.description: verifySignup: $guest = matchGuest($contact); forceFill(['guest_id' => $guest->id, ...])
all member reads are keyed on $a->guest_id -> full stay history, invoices PDFs, pay links, cancel

intended_control: OTP proves control of the contact; contact must identify exactly one guest
observed_or_expected_result: Attacker registers +44xxx123456789 and is linked to a Cameroonian guest +237 123456789 (9 significant digits) -> sees and cancels that guest's bookings, downloads invoices
conditions: a staff-created guest whose phone has the same last 9 digits exists in the group
guest has no verified member account yet (profile_taken check)
smallest_fix: Match on the full E.164-normalised number (or require country code equality); when several guests match, do not auto-link (create a new profile and let staff merge)
regression_test_idea: Seed guest phone '+237650000001'; register member with '+33650000001' and verify -> account.guest_id must be a new guest, not the seeded one

title: Idempotency-Key replay cache for unauthenticated routes is keyed only by key|method|path, so any client can replay another client's stored response
boundary_crossed: Client-to-client (and potentially group-to-group since path includes group slug only for booking routes)

sink.description: returns stored response_body (e.g. booking confirmation with manage_token, pay-link intent) when key and request_hash match

propagation.description: request_hash must match too, which makes exploitation need the identical body - practical only for low-entropy bodies (e.g. /payments/callbacks, /booking/{group}/reservations/cancel {confirmation, token})

intended_control: Idempotency keys are meant to be per client
observed_or_expected_result: Mostly informational: a victim's response is replayable only with identical body; realistic abuse limited to replaying cancel/callback outcomes. Noted for completeness.
conditions: attacker knows key + exact body
smallest_fix: Include client IP (or skip caching) for anonymous requests; or require Idempotency-Key only on authenticated routes
regression_test_idea: Two different IPs send same key/body to a public route -> second must not get Idempotent-Replayed:true
